question.text: Mr. Arjun Malhotra, a Mumbai-based tax counsel, is advising an AIF sponsor on the 'tax neutrality' principle in AIF pooling. Which of the following BEST describes tax neutrality as applied to AIF structures?

answer.text: Pooling eliminates all tax liabilities of investors arising from fund income
Pooling shifts tax incidence permanently from the investor to the Manager
Pooling guarantees a minimum post-tax return through use of tax treaties only
Pooling should not put an investor in a comparatively adverse tax position as compared to investing at individual level

explanation.text: The Logic: Tax neutrality means the investor should not be in a comparatively adverse taxation position through the pooled vehicle versus investing at the individual level. It is a design principle, not an elimination of tax or a guarantee of returns. The Trap: Option A exaggerates — pooling never eliminates tax. Option B is wrong because pooling does not permanently shift tax incidence to the Manager. Option C narrows neutrality to tax treaties, which is not the workbook definition. Note: Category I and Category II AIFs are accorded pass-through treatment, whereas Category III AIFs are not — so achieving neutrality is generally harder for Category III.
